stories.title: Trump administration sues to block certification of Alaska election
stories.summary: The Trump administration wants to block the certification of the Senate election in Alaska if Republican Senator Dan Sullivan loses, arguing that another candidate with the same name may confuse voters. The justice department said in a federal lawsuit filed on Thursday that the inclusion of another Dan Sullivan on the ballot could lead some to mistakenly cast their votes for the wrong candidate. Polls suggest the race between Senator Sullivan and Democrat Mary Peltola is tight, with Peltola holding a narrow lead in the final days before the 3 November vote. The US government wants the judge to bar the state from certifying the results if Senator Sullivan loses by a margin less than the other Sullivan.

reserveStories.title: This design software reimagines everyday objects as self-aware devices
reserveStories.summary: MIT researchers developed X-Hinges, software that helps design 3D-printed objects with built-in sensors. The tricky part is separating the sensors’ signals from interference caused by the wire-like connections around them. The tool places two different materials in the design to reduce that interference. The researchers describe objects such as lamps and gloves that respond to touch, as well as small robots and toys. It is an understandable electronics problem: make an object sense what someone is doing, then get a clear signal out of it.
reserveStories.editorialText: As a child, you likely saw a few Disney movies depicting inanimate objects, such as clocks, cups, and toys, as interactive companions to humans — an act of pure magic, seemingly. But scientists at MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL) are now doing something similar: transforming stationary items into self-aware tools that perceive and respond to human motion to complete a task. Engineers have 3D-printed these dynamic items with built-in sensing, using conductive materials for sensors and traces (sort of like wires) inside. The issue: both components were typically fabricated using the same material, so they’d emit similar signals. It’s sort of like hearing two radio stations at the same time, a mixup that’s hard to interpret.
